text.content: Meridian Consulting's agent can now hold a conversation, stay in scope, and remember what was said earlier in a session. What it cannot do is answer questions about Meridian itself.

rich_text.plain_text: Meridian Consulting's agent can now hold a conversation, stay in scope, and remember what was said earlier in a session. What it cannot do is answer questions about Meridian itself.

text.content: Ask it how a Severity 2 issue should be escalated, or what language to use for a deliverable in Poland, and it has nothing to draw on. The system prompt defines how the agent behaves. It does not contain Meridian's internal documentation. Without access to that documentation, the agent can only answer in generalities — useful for a chatbot, useless for a consulting firm.

text.content: The fix is to give the agent its own searchable copy of Meridian's internal documents. When a question comes in, the agent retrieves the most relevant passages and answers from those, instead of from training data alone. This pattern is called retrieval, and the place where the documents live is a Document Store.

text.content: A Document Store is only useful if retrieval actually returns the right passages for a given question. Two things have to work at the same time.

rich_text.plain_text: A Document Store is only useful if retrieval actually returns the right passages for a given question. Two things have to work at the same time.

text.content: The documents are indexed at the right granularity.

rich_text.plain_text: The documents are indexed at the right granularity.

text.content: Chunks need to be small enough that a single chunk is about one thing, and large enough that the thing makes sense on its own. Chunks that are too big mix unrelated policies into one passage; chunks that are too small split a single policy across several passages. Either failure mode degrades retrieval.

text.content: The embedding model produces vectors of a fixed size. The vector store has to be configured to expect that exact size. A mismatch is not a slow failure — the upsert refuses to run.
